Anointing of Christ
uh-NOYNT-ing uv kryst
noun phrase (the Spirit's unction of the Messiah)
From “anoint,” through Old French enoint, from Latin inunctus; the title “Christ” (Greek Christos, “Anointed”) renders the Hebrew Mashiach, Messiah.

📖 Biblical Definition

The anointing of Christ is the consecration of the Lord Jesus by the Holy Ghost for His threefold office as Prophet, Priest, and King. The very name “Christ” (Greek Christos) and “Messiah” (Hebrew Mashiach) mean “the Anointed One,” for under the old covenant prophets, priests, and kings were set apart by the pouring of oil, a sign of the Spirit's equipping. What the oil signified, the Spirit Himself accomplished in Christ without measure. At His baptism the Spirit descended upon Him, and He opened His ministry in the synagogue at Nazareth by reading Isaiah: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor.” Peter declares that God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power, and He went about doing good and healing all that were oppressed of the devil. The Psalm sings that God hath anointed Him with the oil of gladness above His fellows. The dictionary holds that this anointing equipped the incarnate Son in His human nature for His mediatorial work—to teach as the great Prophet, to offer Himself and intercede as the great High Priest, and to rule and subdue as the great King. From His fulness His people receive their anointing, for those who are in Christ are made, in their measure, prophets, priests, and kings to God, sharing by the same Spirit in the unction of their Head.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The consecration of the Lord Jesus by the Holy Ghost for His threefold office of Prophet, Priest, and King; the name “Christ” itself means “the Anointed,” and from His fulness His people receive their anointing.

expand to see more

ANOINTING OF CHRIST, noun phrase. The Spirit's consecration of the Lord Jesus for His mediatorial office.

“Christ” (Greek Christos) and “Messiah” (Hebrew Mashiach) both mean “the Anointed One.”

God anointed Him with the Holy Ghost and with power (Acts 10:38).

It equipped Him as Prophet to teach, Priest to offer and intercede, and King to rule.

From His fulness His people receive their anointing by the same Spirit.

📖 Key Scripture

Lu 4:18 — "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised,"

Ac 10:38 — "How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil; for God was with him."

Ps 45:7 — "Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows."

Isa 61:1 — "The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound;"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The charismatic counterfeit detaches “the anointing” from Christ and His office and turns it into a transferable power or aura claimed by self-styled apostles and healers.

expand to see more

Modern charismatic and word-of-faith teaching has made “the anointing” a free-floating commodity—a power, an aura, a mantle that gifted men possess and impart, often for gain. The dictionary names this as a corruption of the biblical doctrine. The anointing in Scripture is first and supremely the consecration of Christ for His office by the Spirit; what believers receive is a share in His unction, the indwelling Spirit who teaches and seals them, not a transferable energy to be claimed, marketed, or manipulated. The New Apostolic Reformation's talk of “the anointing” severed from Christ's mediatorial work is a counterfeit.

The recovery is the threefold office. Christ was anointed Prophet, Priest, and King, and His people, united to Him, share in that anointing in their measure: they know the truth by His prophetic teaching, they draw near to God by His priestly sacrifice, and they reign over sin by His kingly power (Heidelberg Catechism, Q. 32). The believer's anointing is the indwelling Spirit applying the benefits of Christ, not a badge of spiritual celebrity. The dictionary roots all true anointing in the Anointed One and rebukes every detached and mercenary counterfeit.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew mashach (to anoint) and its noun Mashiach (Messiah), rendered in Greek by chrio (to anoint) and Christos (Christ); both name the Spirit-consecrated One.

expand to see more

Mashach, Hebrew, to anoint or smear with oil, the rite of setting apart to office.

Mashiach, Hebrew, “Anointed One,” whence “Messiah.”

Chrio, Greek, to anoint; Christos, “the Anointed,” whence “Christ.”

The anointing oil of the old covenant figured the Spirit's equipping for office.

Chrisma, Greek, the “unction” believers have from the Holy One (1 John 2:20).

Usage

"The teacher showed that “Christ” means “the Anointed,” consecrated by the Spirit as Prophet, Priest, and King."

"He rebuked the notion of a transferable “anointing,” for the believer's unction is a share in Christ's."

"She rejoiced that, being in the Anointed, she too was made by the Spirit a prophet, priest, and king to God."
